vignette: John is a 71-year-old security guard who has been struggling with intense distress following an incident of terrorism. John’s trauma began when he was working his night shift at a local shopping center in New York City. He recalls the day vividly: a masked individual entered the premises, brandishing a weapon and demanding money from the customers and employees alike. The assailant moved swiftly through the crowd, shouting threats and firing shots into the air. John’s memories of this event are exceptionally clear; he can replay every detail in his mind—the sound of gunshots, the terrified faces of the shoppers, and the feeling of utter helplessness. John's self-reported symptoms have significantly impacted his life since then. He always sits with his back against a wall to maintain a full view of the room, vigilant for any signs of danger. This hypervigilance towards people is especially heightened when he is in public spaces or at work. Sometimes, John finds himself ruminating about how to exact revenge on the assailant, replaying scenarios in his mind where he confronts and retaliates against the individual who caused him such trauma. Despite these vivid memories, there are moments when John feels completely numb, as if the event happened to someone else entirely. This emotional detachment is paired with an inability to form a coherent narrative of what transpired that night. The inconsistency in how he processes his traumatic experience has left him feeling disconnected and confused about his own role in the incident. John's negative appraisals further exacerbate his distress. He feels deeply incapable of coping with even minor upsets, which only heightens his sense of vulnerability. Additionally, he often compares himself to others, believing that someone else would have handled the situation differently or avoided it altogether. This self-criticism has led him to feel as though he has failed in his most important role—keeping people safe. In John's daily life, these symptoms manifest through specific behaviors and consequences. His need for constant vigilance at work has strained his relationships with colleagues, who find his paranoia concerning and disruptive. He avoids social gatherings and public events due to the fear of encountering dangerous individuals, leading to a sense of isolation from friends and family. At home, John’s marriage has also been affected. He often finds himself in a state of rumination about revenge, which leaves little room for open communication with his wife. His wife notices that he is distant and preoccupied much of the time, and this emotional disconnection has caused significant tension in their relationship. Despite these challenges, what finally brought John to seek help was an incident where his hypervigilance at work led to a minor altercation with a customer who he mistakenly perceived as threatening. The realization that his symptoms were affecting not only himself but also those around him prompted him to consider professional assistance. John is most afraid of the possibility of reliving the trauma and feeling helpless once again, unable to protect others or even himself. However, he is hopeful that through therapy, he can regain some semblance of control over his life and find a way to reconcile the fragmented pieces of his traumatic memory. In seeking help, John hopes to re-establish a sense of safety and security in his daily activities and interactions with those around him. He wants to understand why these memories persist so vividly while also feeling disconnected from them at times. Ultimately, he is eager to find a path forward that allows him to reclaim his role as a protective figure without being consumed by the trauma of that night.
